stonewll123 I am a somewhat new user to GrapheneOS

Welcome! We hope you'll enjoy your stay.

stonewll123 I see androidauto connects just fine but will not display the apps I want.

Apps need to be programmed by their developers to detect & properly connect with Android Auto (AA). Not all apps will be. I don't know what apps you're using, but some apps that you might wish to show up in AA simply won't because the developers haven't programmed in the capability. Whether that's an issue with your apps, I do not know. Just something to be aware of.

Since you're using the Aurora Store, another thing to be aware of is that by default AA only lists & allows apps that have been installed / updated from the Google Play Store. If you want your apps from other sources to show up, you'll need to enable apps from unknown sources inside AA. Here are the steps to do so.

• Navigate to Settings > Apps > Sandboxed Google Play > Android Auto > Android Auto settings

• Scroll down & tap Version

• Tap Version and permission info 8 times

• Accept the pop-up

• Scroll back up to the top of AA's settings

• Tap the three dots in the upper right corner

• Select Developer settings in the pop-up menu

• Scroll down the list & enable Unknown sources

• Restart AA

Now your apps should show up in AA the next time you connect to your car. But, as an important note, apps within the "navigation category" (as defined by Google) are prevented from working if they haven't been installed from the Play Store, even with unknown sources enabled inside AA. So your media & messages will show up fine, but navigation apps such as CoMaps won't work if installed from the Aurora Store or through Obtainium. Nothing we can do about that, unfortunately. It's just more anticompetitive behavior from Google.

Good luck.
